A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DADA research work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, fine-tuning experiments, parameter sensitivity studies, and appendix results including UCR evaluation.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds masking experiments, training-contamination tests, runtime comparisons, and additional visual analyses.

M1.justification: The complementary masking, adaptive bottleneck routing, dual adversarial decoders, training objectives, and variance-based anomaly scoring are retained. Section 3.2 clarifies patch embeddings, mask dimensions, and the reconstruction pipeline; the expanded anomaly-injection description documents existing components rather than establishing a changed method.

E1.justification: All named pre-training and downstream datasets, including UCR, are retained. Appendix E.8 adds a contaminated-training scenario in which injected anomalies are treated as normal pre-training data. GECCO and Creditcard enter additional MoE analyses but were already evaluated elsewhere in v3.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged. However, Appendix E.4 replaces the single-versus-multiple-bottleneck timing comparison with comparisons against A.T., ModernTCN, GPT4TS, and multi-domain-pretrained GPT4TS. The new PSM case study also introduces GPT4TS and ModernTCN into that qualitative comparison.

E3.justification: The principal splits, metrics, training budget, and zero-shot protocol are retained. New analyses introduce complementary-mask ratios from 10/90 to 50/50, controlled training contamination, and SMD per-epoch training and single-forward-pass timing. Table 4 changes the reported SWaT dimensionality from 51 to 31 without establishing that experiments were rerun; its MSL/SMAP corrections align with single-channel preprocessing already stated in v3.

E4.justification: Appendices E.7-E.9 add ordinary-versus-complementary masking, mask-ratio sensitivity, contamination robustness, and training-loss analysis. E.1 adds a comparative PSM case study, and E.3 extends the bottleneck/MoE analysis to GECCO and Creditcard. These substantially expand scrutiny of the method. The original isolated bottleneck-overhead experiment is removed and replaced by cross-model timing.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The additional tables and loss curves do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Substantial new results cover masking, contamination, runtime, expanded MoE comparisons, and qualitative behavior. For example, Table 14 reports mean F1 decreasing from 78.26 without contamination to 76.64 at 10%. DADA's headline scores remain unchanged. Table 1 revises A.T.'s SMD F1 from 66.42 to 69.46, D3R's SMD/SWaT values from 78.02/74.39 to 78.04/74.41, and GPT4TS's SMD value from 83.13 to 83.14. Some appendix tables retain the earlier baseline values.

T1.justification: The substantive mathematics in Equations (1)-(7) is retained. Dimension-symbol edits, patch-mask notation, and the explicit composition defining Recon clarify the existing formulation. Neither version provides theoretical propositions or proofs that are added, removed, or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: multi-domain pre-training enables one model to perform zero-shot anomaly detection, adaptive bottlenecks accommodate differing data requirements, and adversarial decoders improve normal/anomalous discrimination with competitive downstream performance.

C2.justification: v4 explains how directly maximizing abnormal reconstruction loss can produce arbitrary decoder outputs and undermine normal-pattern learning. It expands the MoE interpretation around dataset-specific bottleneck preferences and adds interpretations concerning balanced masking, contamination tolerance, and adversarial training stability. The runtime discussion acknowledges ModernTCN's faster inference while distinguishing its downstream training requirement.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code repository link, explains the existing anomaly transformations and random non-overlapping injection procedure, cites injection defaults, and first states that testing retains the final partial batch. Table 4 corrects MSL/SMAP dimensionality to match existing prose. Conversely, replacing Appendix E.4 removes the explicit description of bottlenecks as lightweight MLPs. These documentation changes do not establish corresponding implementation changes.

R1.justification: v4 adds references including MultiRC, CATCH, AutoTSAD, sparsely gated MoE, and TFB, while removing some earlier citations such as LoOP and the Tang outlier-detection works. The central positioning around general, zero-shot time-series anomaly detection remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the overall section sequence are retained. Local revisions clarify Section 3.2, expand anomaly-injection explanations, rewrite parts of the MoE and timing discussions, and append E.7-E.9. Conference publication text and acknowledgments are also added.

P2.justification: The appendix displays substantially expand through four new tables (11-14), a comparative PSM visualization (Figure 11), and loss curves (Figure 13). Table 10 gains two dataset columns and Table 9 gains a metric row. The original Figure 11 is retained as Figure 12. Existing diagrams largely retain their design, while Figure 2 and Table 2 are relocated and conference headers are added.

improvement.justification: v4 provides useful evidence about complementary masking and contaminated normal training data, and makes the existing injection and testing procedures clearer. The gains are limited by removal of the isolated bottleneck-overhead check, inconsistent baseline scores between Table 1 and Tables 8/11, and an apparent MSL/SMAP heading reversal in Table 13. The added validation and reproducibility information nevertheless support a modest overall improvement.
